Term (Article 156):
• Five years
• Holds office during the pleasure of the President

Removal:
• No impeachment process
• Removed by the President at will

This makes the Governor different from the President.

rows: Removed by President at will (No impeachment)
Holds office during the pleasure of the President
Fixed term protected by constitutional safeguards

items: Article 156 is frequently asked regarding the term and pleasure of the President.
Exams often test whether a Governor undergoes impeachment—remember, there is NO impeachment process for a Governor.
The Governor can be removed by the President at will, unlike the President who requires a formal constitutional procedure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 156 prescribes the term of office for the Governor.
The normal tenure of a Governor is five years, but it is not fixed.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
No formal impeachment process is required for the removal of a Governor.
The President has the power to remove a Governor at will.
